title: No black musicians in Dorsey's band; Shavers and Teddy Wilson
summary: Leeman says Charlie Shavers was the first black musician Dorsey hired, years after Teddy Wilson and Lionel Hampton joined Goodman, helped by John Hammond.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You were with Tommy Dorsey's band with Charlie Shavers.
No, that was after -- yes, I did, I played on and off with Tommy for 18 years.
But with Charlie Shavers, I'm trying to find out about Charlie Shavers.
That was later, much later.
It was several years later that Charlie Shavers came into the band.
Yes.
Then there were no black musicians in the band when you were there.
No.
So evidently, it was Benny Goodman that --
Sy Oliver was another Jimmie Mundy came with us.
Well, he arranged, but he never appeared as a musician.
No. No, no black musicians -- Charlie Shavers was the first black musician Tommy ever hired.
Right. And was he hired after Benny Goodman had hired Teddy Wilson?
Teddy and Lionel were from '38 on -- they were already with Benny Goodman.
Yes, but Teddy Wilson was the first black musician to be hired by a white band. That's a matter of record, I believe.
I think so, just about.
Yeah, I think so.
And then Benny saw that things were working out good, I think, giving credit where credit was due.
Yeah, absolutely. No question about that.
Oh, what was his name ...
: John Hammond.
Yes, John Hammond.
(CUT)
(END OF PROCEEDINGS AS RECORDED)
